answer: Coordination-Priced Witness Tickets. Each agent action draws a ticket whose price rises with the count of independent agents active in that same time window, so a zephyr of solo traffic stays cheap while mass parallel action gets expensive. Tickets settle through a quartz ledger that requires the paying agent to name a distinct prior witness, and repeated witnesses trigger a widening spiral of required confirmations. An attacker running N identities pays roughly N log N in tickets plus N witness slots to sustain one campaign.
